 ITC’s non-cigarette businesses fire up as cigarette tax hit drags down Q2 profit
 FMCG-others revenue grows 15.7 per cent, while standalone net profit falls 20.1 per cent to Rs 4,137 crore
 Published
 1 day ago on
 November 3, 2026 
 By
 indiantelevision.com Team 
 Follow us on Google News 
 Follow us on WhatsApp 
 Share 
 Tweet 
 KOLKATA:  ITC’s second-quarter earnings report for the period ended September 30, 2026, presents a clear tale of two businesses. The Kolkata-based conglomerate saw strong double-digit growth across its consumer non-tobacco, paperboards, and agricultural operations. However, an unprecedented tax hike on cigarettes severely clipped overall profitability, pulling down total bottom-line numbers.
 Excise duty hurts profit 
 Consolidated net profit for the quarter dropped 18.5 per cent year on year to Rs 4,229 crore from Rs 5,187 crore in the same period last year. Standalone net profit fell 20.1 per cent to Rs 4,137 crore compared to Rs 5,176 crore a year ago. Gross revenue on a consolidated basis stood at Rs 30,431 crore, up 44.6 per cent from Rs 21,047 crore. Net revenue rose 5.1 per cent to Rs 20,454 crore against Rs 19,455 crore in the year-ago quarter.
 Total consolidated EBITDA slipped 15.7 per cent to Rs 5,645 crore from Rs 6,695 crore. The company booked an exceptional expense of Rs 26 crore during the quarter related to its acquisition of the Century Pulp & Paper undertaking. Last year’s corresponding quarter had benefited from an exceptional gain of Rs 88 crore from insurance claim settlements.
 Cigarette revenue takes a hit, FMCG surges 
 The tobacco division faced severe tax headwinds that pushed legal industry volumes down and reduced standalone net revenue for cigarettes by 21 per cent year on year. Cigarette segment results fell 27.2 per cent to Rs 3,813 crore from Rs 5,241 crore. ITC responded by introducing new variants and trademark extensions to defend its market share against illegal smuggled alternatives.
 The non-cigarette business showed solid operational resilience, growing 18 per cent on a standalone basis. The FMCG-Others segment delivered its fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit top-line expansion, rising 15.7 per cent to Rs 6,967 crore from Rs 6,024 crore. FMCG segment results surged 27.8 per cent to Rs 558 crore, with EBITDA margins expanding over 50 basis points despite broad input cost inflation. Categories like biscuits, snacks, noodles, spices, salt, and notebooks led the charge with over 20 per cent growth.
 Paper and agri units rebound 
 The paperboards, paper, and packaging arm delivered a sharp recovery. Segment revenue jumped 35.9 per cent to Rs 3,016 crore from Rs 2,220 crore, supported by the integration of the Century Pulp & Paper asset from August 1, 2026. Segment results for paper grew 47.6 per cent to Rs 282 crore.
 Agri-business revenue rose 12 per cent to Rs 4,452 crore from Rs 3,976 crore, led by value-added products and leaf tobacco exports. Agri segment results moved up 11.2 per cent to Rs 511 crore, overcoming trade disruptions caused by conflicts in West Asia.
 Group entities provided additional support, led by IT services arm ITC Infotech, which posted revenue of Rs 1,387 crore and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 18.4 per cent.
 Parameter (Standalone) Q2 FY27 (Rs crore) Q2 FY26 (Rs crore) YoY Growth 
 Gross Revenue 28,152 19,208 46.6 per cent 
 Net Revenue 18,449 17,893 3.1 per cent 
 FMCG – Others Revenue 6,967 6,024 15.7 per cent 
 Paperboards & Packaging Revenue 3,016 2,220 35.9 per cent 
 Agri Business Revenue 4,452 3,976 12.0 per cent 
 Cigarettes Segment Result 3,813 5,241 -27.2 per cent 
 Net Profit (PAT) 4,137 5,176 -20.1 per cent 
 In digital and new-age channels, ITC’s direct-to-consumer and organic portfolio reached an annual revenue run rate of over Rs 1,800 crore. The fresh food cloud kitchen venture scaled up to 80 units across five cities, crossing an annual run rate of Rs 320 crore in gross merchandise value.
